item.title: Leaked clips reveal Google's Gemini Omni video model ahead of I/O 2026
item.description: A new AI video generation model called Gemini Omni has surfaced inside Google's Gemini app in two waves of leaks, setting the stage for what could be a major announcement at Google I/O 2026 on May 19.

item.title: Iran threatens weapons-grade uranium enrichment as ceasefire frays
item.description: The fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran entered its most precarious phase yet after President Donald Trump rejected Tehran's 14-point counterproposal on Sunday, calling it "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" and likening the truce to a patient with "about a 1 percent chance of survival." Iran responded with defiance, as parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared on Tuesday that the United States "has no alternative" but to accept the terms, and a senior lawmaker warned Tehran could enrich uranium to weapons-grade 90% purity if hostilities resume.

item.title: Iran redefines Strait of Hormuz as 500-km military zone
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy announced on Tuesday that it has fundamentally redefined the Strait of Hormuz, expanding its claimed operational zone from a narrow waterway to a vast 500-kilometer military corridor — the latest escalation in the ongoing standoff with the United States over control of the world's most critical oil chokepoint.

item.title: Starmer tells cabinet he won't quit as rivals circle
item.description:
As Prime Minister Keir Starmer told his cabinet on Tuesday morning that he would not resign, the jockeying to replace him has already begun in earnest — with Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham leading betting markets despite not holding a seat in Parliament.

Starmer's defiant stance came during a tense cabinet meeting at which he challenged internal critics to formally trigger a leadership contest rather than lobby for his departure behind closed doors. "The Labour Party has a procedure for challenging a leader, and that has not been initiated," he said, according to his office. "The nation expects us to continue governing."

item.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum rules out US extraction of indicted Sinaloa governor
item.description:
Mexican Senator Lilly Téllez publicly accused President Claudia Sheinbaum of protecting officials indicted by a U.S. federal court for alleged ties to the Sinaloa Cartel, escalating a political crisis that has tested the bilateral relationship between Washington and Mexico City since late April.

Téllez, a member of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), appeared Sunday on Fox News's "Fox & Friends Weekend," where she claimed Sheinbaum is refusing to hand over indicted officials because doing so would expose deeper corruption within the ruling Morena party. "She's afraid that if she extradites these narco-politicians, the Pandora's box will be open, and many other narco-politicians will fall," Téllez said, calling Mexico a "mafiocracy" governed by "the rule of the mafia".

item.title: WHO raises hantavirus cruise ship cases to 11, warns more likely
item.description: The hantavirus outbreak tied to the MV Hondius cruise ship expanded on Tuesday as Spain confirmed a new case among its repatriated passengers and the World Health Organization raised the global tally to 11 confirmed and suspected infections, including three deaths. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warned during a press briefing in Madrid that more cases are likely, given the virus's long incubation period and the close contact among passengers before the outbreak was identified.

item.title: Altman testifies Musk sought control of OpenAI before departure
item.description:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman took the witness stand on Tuesday in a federal courtroom in Oakland, California, pushing back against Elon Musk's claims that he betrayed the AI company's founding nonprofit mission. Altman testified that it was Musk who sought long-term control of OpenAI and who had advocated for it to merge with Tesla before his departure from the organization in 2018.

"My belief is he wanted to have long term control, and that he would have had that had we agreed to the structure he wanted," Altman said. His testimony, delivered during the third week of the high-profile trial, aimed to counter Musk's assertion that no individual should dominate the future of artificial intelligence and to show that Musk himself was supportive of OpenAI becoming a commercial enterprise.

item.title: Saudi Arabia launched covert strikes on Iran during war
item.description: Saudi Arabia carried out numerous unpublicized military strikes against Iran in late March, according to an exclusive Reuters report published on Tuesday, citing two Western officials and two Iranian officials with knowledge of the operations. The revelation adds a previously unknown dimension to the broader conflict, showing that the kingdom directly struck Iranian territory even as it publicly maintained a defensive posture.

item.title: Kuwait accuses Iran of armed attack on China-funded port island
item.description:
Kuwait accused Iran on Tuesday of dispatching an armed paramilitary Revolutionary Guard team to launch a failed attack on Bubiyan Island, home to a China-funded port project, adding a new layer of tension just as President Donald Trump departed Washington for a state visit to Beijing.

The allegation, carried in a report by the Associated Press, said a team of six armed members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps attempted to infiltrate the island in the northwest corner of the Persian Gulf near Iraq and Iran on May 1. Kuwait said it detained four of the men — identified as two Guard naval captains, a Guard naval lieutenant, and a Guard army lieutenant — while two others escaped when Kuwaiti forces disrupted the infiltration. One Kuwaiti security official was wounded.

Kuwait said the team had planned to carry out "hostile acts" but did not elaborate. The incident was first announced on May 3 without details; Kuwait provided no explanation for the delay in publicly linking it to Iran. Iran did not immediately acknowledge the allegation.

item.title: Mexico denies CNN report of CIA car bombing on its soil
item.description: CNN reported on Tuesday that the CIA has been escalating covert operations inside Mexico, including a car bombing earlier this spring that killed a mid-level Sinaloa Cartel operative on a busy highway near Mexico City. Mexican authorities swiftly and forcefully denied the account, reasserting the country's sovereignty over security matters on its territory.

item.title: US and China agreed to oppose Iran's Strait of Hormuz tolls, State Dept. says
item.description: The United States and China have found rare common ground in opposing Iran's demands to impose tolls on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the State Department confirmed on Tuesday, offering a potential diplomatic opening ahead of this week's summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

item.title: Iran restored 30 of 33 Hormuz missile sites, US intel finds
item.description: Classified U.S. intelligence assessments show that Iran has regained operational access to 30 of its 33 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz and retains roughly 70 percent of its prewar missile stockpile, according to reporting by The New York Times on Monday, sharply undercutting the Trump administration's repeated assertions that the Iranian military had been "decimated."

item.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for first China visit since 2017
item.description: President Donald Trump departed Washington on Tuesday for a state visit to China, arriving in Beijing on Wednesday evening for his first trip to the country since 2017 and the first by any sitting U.S. president in nearly nine years. Over the next two days, Trump will hold formal talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping on issues spanning trade, Taiwan, rare earth minerals, artificial intelligence, and the ongoing war in Iran.

item.title: Gunshots erupt at Philippine Senate during ICC arrest standoff
item.description:
Gunfire broke out at the Philippine Senate on Wednesday evening as military and law enforcement personnel moved into the building to apprehend Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of crimes against humanity linked to former President Rodrigo Duterte's deadly anti-drug campaign.

The identity of those who fired the shots remained unclear as journalists and bystanders scrambled for cover amid the chaos, according to Reuters. The incident marks a dramatic escalation in a standoff that has gripped the country since the ICC unsealed its arrest warrant on Monday.

item.title: Trump lands in Beijing, demands China 'open up' to US business
item.description:
President Donald Trump landed in Beijing on Wednesday for a high-stakes state visit, bringing with him a delegation of more than a dozen of America's most powerful corporate executives and a blunt message for Chinese leader Xi Jinping: "open up" China to American firms.

Trump, who was greeted on the tarmac by Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, a military honor guard, and some 300 flag-waving youths, told reporters aboard Air Force One that market access for U.S. businesses would be his first request when formal talks begin. The summit meetings are scheduled for Thursday and Friday at the Great Hall of the People, with a visit to the Temple of Heaven and a state banquet also planned.

item.title: Streeting prepares to resign and challenge Starmer for Labour leadership
item.description: Health Secretary Wes Streeting is preparing to resign from the cabinet as early as Thursday to mount a formal leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer, according to a report in The Times. The move, which would represent the most direct threat yet to Starmer's premiership, came after Streeting held a brief meeting with the Prime Minister on Wednesday morning ahead of the King's Speech.

item.title: Australia joins UK-France naval mission to secure Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
The United Kingdom and France hosted a multinational meeting of defense ministers on Tuesday to advance plans for a naval mission to protect commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as Australia confirmed it would join the effort and Britain deployed a warship to the region.

UK Defence Secretary John Healey and French Armed Forces Minister Catherine Vautrin co-chaired the virtual meeting, which brought together representatives from more than 40 countries to discuss military contributions to the European-led coalition. The talks came as Iran issued sharp warnings against any foreign naval presence in the waterway.

item.title: Truck convoys across Arabia become lifeline amid Hormuz closure
item.description:
Convoys of heavy-duty trucks barreling across the Arabian desert have become an unlikely escape valve for the global economy, as the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz forces Gulf states to improvise new land routes for energy and commodity shipments, according to a report published Monday by The Wall Street Journal.

The truck convoys represent one piece of a broader scramble by Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Oman to keep trade flowing more than two months after Iran effectively shut down the world's most important oil chokepoint in late February, in retaliation for U.S. and Israeli strikes. Before the closure, roughly 20 million barrels of crude oil passed through the strait daily. Traffic has since collapsed to about 5% of pre-war levels, according to maritime data firm Kpler.

item.title: Iran says Hormuz control could double its oil revenues
item.description: Iranian Army Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia declared on Wednesday that Tehran's strategic grip over the Strait of Hormuz could generate revenues exceeding twice the country's oil income, as Iran deepens its efforts to formalize control over the world's most vital oil chokepoint amid its ongoing war with the United States and Israel.

item.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for summit with Xi amid Iran war tensions
item.description:
President Donald Trump touched down in Beijing on Wednesday for a high-stakes summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, arriving against the backdrop of a fragile ceasefire in the Iran conflict and deep uncertainty over whether the two superpowers can find common ground on the Middle East, trade, and Taiwan.

The visit — the first by a U.S. president to China since Trump's own trip in November 2017 — had originally been scheduled for late March but was postponed due to the outbreak of war with Iran in late February. Trump was greeted with a red-carpet welcome ceremony, with Chinese and American flags waved in rhythmic unison by uniformed greeters, according to the Associated Press. The formal bilateral talks between Trump and Xi are set to begin Thursday and extend through Friday.
